topic: Typographic and color system specification for satishregonda.in — three defensible type pairings (verified from font binaries: licensing, OpenType features, figure behavior, real file sizes) and three WCAG-verified light/dark color palettes anchored in IPCC AR6 climate colormaps, plus spacing, grid, radii, shadow, focus and link-styling rules.
key_findings: GOOGLE FONTS SILENTLY STRIPS OPENTYPE FEATURES — verified by diffing Adobe's upstream release against the Google-served woff2. Upstream Source Serif 4 VAR exposes aalt c2sc case ccmp dnom frac kern liga lnum locl mark mkmk numr onum ordn pnum sinf smcp ss01 ss02 subs sups tnum zero. The Google latin subset exposes ONLY ccmp dnom frac kern liga locl mark mkmk numr pnum tnum. Thirteen features removed, including smcp, c2sc, onum, lnum, zero. Google also strips the license string (nameID 13) from every family checked. Small caps and oldstyle figures — the two features that most make an academic site look editorially crafted — are unavailable unless you self-host upstream.

TABULAR-BY-DEFAULT vs NEEDS-tnum, measured from actual digit advance widths. Tabular by default (all ten digits identical width, publication years align with zero CSS): Source Serif 4 (500/1000), Spectral (500/1000), Newsreader (1100/2000), EB Garamond (480/1000), Charis SIL (1153/2048), Gentium Book Plus (986/2048), Switzer (576/1000), IBM Plex Serif/Sans/Mono (600/1000). Proportional but has tnum: Literata, Lora, Crimson Pro, Petrona, Bitter, Public Sans, Karla, Work Sans, Geist, Inter, Instrument Sans, Space Grotesk, Schibsted Grotesk, Faustina, Vollkorn, Alegreya, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. Has NEITHER (unusable for publication tables): Libre Baskerville, Libre Franklin, Fraunces, Instrument Serif, and Fontshare's Erode, Supreme, Bespoke Serif, Synonym, Gambetta.

THE FONTSHARE LICENSE NOW BANS SUBSETTING. ITF Free Font License (FFL) v2.0, dated 17 Aug 2026, read verbatim from Switzer_Complete/License/FFL.txt inside the download. Section 01 permits self-hosting: 'You may self-host the Font Software on your own servers or infrastructure ... including through standard webfont technologies such as CSS @font-face.' But Section 02 prohibits modification 'including modifying or replacing glyphs, subsetting, format conversion, or altering font names', and the Derivative Work definition explicitly names 'subsetting, format conversion'. You may ship Fontshare's own .woff2 byte-for-byte but may NOT run a subsetter or converter over it. Governed by Indian law, exclusive jurisdiction Ahmedabad. The opposite of SIL OFL, which explicitly permits modification.

SELF-HOSTING SOURCE SERIF 4 IS BOTH SMALLER AND MORE CAPABLE THAN GOOGLE FONTS. Measured: Google's css2 endpoint serves roman+italic variable (opsz 8-60, wght 200-900, latin) at 246.2 KB with features stripped. Self-hosting the upstream OTF subset to Latin, keeping the full feature list, with opsz pinned at 20 and wght left variable = 67.5 KB roman + 53.1 KB italic = 120.6 KB. 51% fewer bytes AND it keeps small caps, oldstyle figures and zero-slash. Keeping opsz variable costs 162.2 KB roman + 131.6 KB italic.

NARROWING A GOOGLE FONTS AXIS RANGE DOES NOT REDUCE PAYLOAD. Measured on Source Serif 4 roman, latin subset: `opsz,wght@8..60,400..600` = 119.3 KB and `opsz,wght@8..60,200..900` = 119.3 KB — byte-identical. Only pinning to a single static weight changes it (`@8..60,400` = 47.4 KB); two static weights (400;600) = 99.5 KB. The common optimization of writing a tight range in the Google URL buys nothing.

INTER IS THE #5 MOST-USED FAMILY ON GOOGLE FONTS. From the live metadata endpoint: Roboto 2, Open Sans 3, Google Sans 4, Inter 5, Montserrat 7, Poppins 8, Lato 9. Of the top 30 families only two are serifs (Playfair Display 26, Roboto Slab 29). Inter-alone is the strongest 'this is a default' signal available; leading with a serif places the site outside the visual mode of 28 of the 30 most-used web families.

IPCC AR6 PUBLISHES OFFICIAL CLIMATE-SCIENCE COLOR VALUES AND WATER IS NOT BLUE. From github.com/IPCC-WG1/colormaps (master). The precipitation sequential ramp runs #FFFFE5 (dry cream) to #003C30 (deep teal-green) via #56A89D, #35978F, #2C877F, #21746B, #166157, #1A695F. The precipitation divergent ramp is brown-to-teal: #543005 through #F8F8F7 to #003C30. Sea level is a separate navy ramp #FEFEFE to #00054A via #2E5995, #234A8B, #436F9D. The defensible 'water' accent for a hydrology site is dark TEAL-GREEN — the exact hue the IPCC uses to mean 'wetter'.

IPCC's categorical palette 'gree-blue_cat' is Paul Tol's colorblind-safe qualitative set verbatim: #332288, #117733, #88CCEE, #999933, #44AA99, #6699CC. Use this for charts rather than inventing a series palette. The IPCC style guide convention is blue for water, green for biomass, red for temperature, and it warns against blue/purple and green/red pairings in divergent schemes for colorblind readers.

GWERN.NET — the most typographically obsessive long-form site on the web — RUNS THE STACK I AM RECOMMENDING. From https://gwern.net/static/css/head.css: `--GW-serif-font-stack: "Source Serif 4", "Apple Garamond", "Baskerville", ...`; `--GW-sans-serif-font-stack: "Source Sans 3", ...`; `--GW-monospaced-font-stack: "IBM Plex Mono", ...`. It also uses font-variant-caps: small-caps and font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums / lining-nums / tabular-nums — i.e. the self-hosted upstream build, not Google's.

GWERN DOCUMENTS A NON-OBVIOUS TRAP WITH OLDSTYLE FIGURES IN LINKS. Verbatim CSS comment: '/* Disable oldstyle nums in underlined links because the oldstyle nums are almost subscript-like and overlap */' followed by `font-variant-numeric: lining-nums;` on the link rule. Oldstyle figures descend below the baseline and collide with the underline. On a publication list where nearly every entry is a link containing a year, this would be visible everywhere. He also builds underlines as a 1px linear-gradient background at `calc(100% - 0.1em)` plus a text-shadow halo in the page background color, rather than text-decoration, for controllable skip-ink.

KIERAN HEALY (Duke sociology, the best-designed sociologist site) uses COMMERCIAL type: stacks resolve to `valkyrie_ot_a` (Matthew Butterick's Valkyrie OT) and `berkeley mono` (Berkeley Graphics). Both paid. That is the aesthetic target; the free equivalents are Source Serif 4 for Valkyrie's sober bookish serif and JetBrains Mono or IBM Plex Mono for Berkeley Mono's engineered grid.

MEASURED OPTICAL-SIZE EQUIVALENCE (x-height/em from OS/2 sxHeight): Source Serif 4 0.475, Newsreader 0.426, Literata 0.507, Spectral 0.450, Crimson Pro 0.420, EB Garamond 0.400, Recia 0.520, Sentient 0.504, Public Sans 0.517, Instrument Sans 0.510, Schibsted Grotesk 0.527, Switzer 0.531, Satoshi 0.500, General Sans 0.538, Geist 0.530, Inter 0.546, JetBrains Mono 0.550, IBM Plex Mono 0.516. To match Source Serif 4 at 18px (x-height 8.55px): Newsreader 20.1px, Literata 16.9px, Recia 16.4px, EB Garamond 21.4px. Pairing a sans at the same nominal px as the serif is always wrong — Public Sans must run at 16.5px against Source Serif 4's 18px.

MEASURED MEASURE — average advance per character over a representative hydrology sentence, as a fraction of em: Newsreader 0.4097, Crimson Pro 0.4047, Spectral 0.4499, Switzer 0.4517, Source Serif 4 0.4562, Karla 0.4618, Geist 0.4691, Public Sans 0.4702, Lora 0.4714, Recia 0.4780, IBM Plex Serif 0.4785, Literata 0.4881, Satoshi 0.4903. A 66-character line is 542px in Source Serif 4 at 18px but 580px in Literata at the same size. A single hardcoded prose max-width is wrong across faces; derive it per face.

FONTSHARE'S SERIFS MOSTLY LACK FIGURE CONTROL, WITH TWO EXCEPTIONS. Measured from the shipped variable woff2 in each package: Recia (34.7 KB roman / 42 KB italic, x-ht 0.520, cap 0.750, wght 300-700) has tnum, pnum, onum, lnum, zero, case — the most complete figure set on Fontshare. Boska (46.2/56 KB, wght 200-900) is the only Fontshare face with real smcp, plus tnum/onum/lnum/case. Erode, Supreme, Bespoke Serif and Synonym expose only `frac` — no figure control at all. Gambetta's OS/2 reports sCapHeight equal to sxHeight (0.450 for both), a metadata bug that breaks cap-height alignment.

FONTSHARE SANS DATA: Switzer variable roman 42.2 KB, x-ht 0.531, cap 0.750, digits uniform 576/1000 — tabular by default despite exposing no tnum, so you get aligned columns but can never get proportional figures for running text. Satoshi 41.6 KB, x-ht 0.500, cap 0.740, wght 300-900, has tnum + pnum + case + ss01 + ss02. General Sans 37.2 KB, x-ht 0.538, has case/ss01/ss02 but NO tnum and non-uniform digits. All are itf_ffl (closed-source, no subsetting); only Azeret Mono and Spline Sans on Fontshare are sil_ofl.

SPECTRAL IS NOT A VARIABLE FONT — Google Fonts metadata lists zero axes; it ships as 14 static styles (200-800 plus italics). Newsreader (opsz 6-72, wght 200-800), Literata (opsz 7-72, wght 200-900) and Source Serif 4 (opsz 8-60, wght 200-900) all have genuine optical-size axes. Instrument Serif is 400/400i only — display use, no text weights.

WCAG 2.2 FOCUS RULES ARE TWO SEPARATE THINGS, OFTEN CONFLATED. SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA) requires the focus indicator to hit 3:1 against adjacent colors — the one you must meet. SC 2.4.13 Focus Appearance is Level AAA and requires area at least equal to a 2 CSS px thick perimeter, plus 3:1 between focused and unfocused states of the same pixels; a 2px outset outline satisfies the area rule, an INSET indicator needs 3px. SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) is the AA criterion about sticky headers covering focused elements — relevant here, since a sticky header hides keyboard focus on anchor targets unless you set scroll-padding-top.
recommendations: ADOPT PAIRING A — 'Gauge': Source Serif 4 for display AND body (exploiting its opsz 8-60 axis), Public Sans for UI/meta, JetBrains Mono for data. Rationale against the brief's four constraints: MINIMAL — one serif superfamily carries display and text, so hierarchy comes from optical size and weight, not from a zoo of faces. EDITORIAL — the opsz axis is the single most editorial move available: set headings at opsz 60 for finer, higher-contrast letterforms and body at opsz 20 for sturdier ones, which is what a real type foundry does and what no template does. SCIENTIFIC — Source Serif 4 is tabular by default, so publication years align with no CSS, and self-hosting restores smcp/onum/zero for venue names and citation counts. INDIAN INSTITUTION — it reads as sober international scholarship rather than costume; the Indian signal belongs in content and in the accent color, not in a decorative typeface. NOT TEMPLATED — it is a serif-led site, and only 2 of the 30 most-used web families are serifs.

SELF-HOST THE FONTS; DO NOT LINK GOOGLE FONTS. Download source-serif-4.004 from github.com/adobe-fonts/source-serif/releases, subset to Latin with fonttools keeping kern,liga,calt,locl,ccmp,mark,mkmk,tnum,pnum,onum,lnum,smcp,c2sc,case,frac,sups,subs,numr,dnom,zero, pin opsz at 20 via fontTools.varLib.instancer, leave wght variable, output woff2. Verified result: 67.5 KB roman + 53.1 KB italic. This is both half the bytes of the Google version and the only way to get small caps and oldstyle figures. Serve from the same origin as the site with `font-display: swap` and a `<link rel=preload as=font crossorigin>` for the roman only.

ADOPT PALETTE A — 'Gauge' (warm paper + IPCC precipitation teal). Light: bg #FBFAF7, surface #F3F1EB, text #1B1A17, text2 #5C5850, text3 #6E6960, hairline #E3DFD5, control-border #8F897D, accent #166157, accent-hover #0E4A42, visited #4A4A6B, accent2 #8A5A24, tint #E4EFEB. Dark: bg #14140F, surface #1D1D18, text #EDEAE2, text2 #A19C90, text3 #8C877C, hairline #2E2E27, control-border #6D685E, accent #6EB4A7, accent-hover #8EC5B5, visited #A8A6C4, accent2 #C8944F, tint #17271F. All 36 text-on-background pairs verified at AA or better; all control borders and focus rings verified at or above 3:1 in both modes against both bg and surface. The accent is lifted directly off the IPCC AR6 precipitation ramp and the secondary accent off the dry end of the same divergent scale, so the two accents are the literal wet/dry poles of the field's own visual language.

SET THE ACCENT BUDGET AT ROUGHLY 2% OF PIXELS AND WRITE IT DOWN AS A RULE. Accent #166157 may be used for exactly five things: (1) inline text links in prose; (2) the active nav item's underline; (3) the focus ring; (4) one thin rule or marker on the current page's section heading; (5) small-caps 'NEW'/'PREPRINT' status tags. It may NOT be used for large filled areas, hero backgrounds, card backgrounds, icons that are not links, or decorative dividers — those all use hairline #E3DFD5 and text2 #5C5850. Accent2 #8A5A24 is reserved for exactly one job: marking outbound links to raftwaters.in and other external destinations. If a page has more than one accent2 mark it is wrong.

PROSE MEASURE: 36rem (576px) for Source Serif 4 at 18px, which is a computed ~70 characters given its measured 0.4562 em average advance. Use a three-tier width system: --w-prose 36rem for running text, --w-content 48rem (768px) for publication lists and student tables that need two columns of metadata, and --w-wide 76rem (1216px) for the full-bleed hero and the RAFT page's image grid. Do not use a single container width; the publication list needs more room than the blog post and hardcoding one number makes both wrong.

LINK STYLING — the single highest-leverage decision on a link-dense academic site. Use `text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 0.06em; text-underline-offset: 0.16em; text-decoration-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 40%, transparent);` on rest, and go to full-opacity accent plus 0.09em thickness on hover. Use em units so the underline scales with the type. Set `text-decoration-skip-ink: auto`. Critically: add `font-variant-numeric: lining-nums;` to the link rule so that oldstyle figures never collide with the underline — this is the exact bug gwern documents, and on a publications page every single link contains a year.

STRIP UNDERLINES ONLY IN THREE PLACES, and give each a different affordance: the nav (active state = 2px accent underline offset 0.4em), the publication list (title links get a hover-only underline, because 60 underlined lines in a row is unreadable), and card links (whole-card hover moves the surface from #FBFAF7 to #F3F1EB). Everywhere else in prose, underline always — academics scan for links and removing them costs more than it gains.

RADII POLICY: 0 almost everywhere. Use --r-0: 0 for cards, section blocks, images and the prose container; --r-1: 2px for tags, chips and code spans; --r-2: 4px only for form inputs and buttons where a hard corner reads as broken; --r-full: 999px for nothing except the avatar. Rounded cards are the loudest single 'template' signal in the current web; hard corners plus a 1px #E3DFD5 hairline is what a printed journal does and it costs nothing.

SHADOW POLICY: no shadows on static content, ever. Structure comes from hairlines and from the surface/background split. Allow exactly two shadows, both only on transient overlaid layers: --shadow-pop `0 1px 2px rgb(27 26 23 / 0.06), 0 4px 12px rgb(27 26 23 / 0.08)` for the mobile nav drawer and any dropdown, and --shadow-modal `0 8px 40px rgb(27 26 23 / 0.16)` for a lightboxed figure. In dark mode replace both with a 1px --hairline top border instead of a shadow, because shadows are invisible on #14140F and the border is what actually reads as elevation.

FOCUS RING: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }` plus a global `:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none; }`. Verified 6.98:1 against bg and 6.45:1 against surface in light, 7.70:1 and 7.05:1 in dark — comfortably past the 3:1 that SC 1.4.11 requires. Use outset (not inset) so the 2px thickness satisfies SC 2.4.13's area rule. Add `html { scroll-padding-top: 5rem; }` so the sticky header does not obscure the focused anchor target, which is what SC 2.4.11 is about.

GRID: a 12-column grid at >=1024px with 24px gutters inside --w-wide 76rem; collapse to 6 columns at 768-1023px with 20px gutters; single column below 768px with 20px page margins. But run prose OUT of the grid — set the article container to `max-width: var(--w-prose); margin-inline: auto` and let only figures, tables and the RAFT image strip opt into full grid width via a `.bleed` utility. Academic pages are 90% single-column text; imposing the grid on paragraphs buys nothing and fights the measure.

SPACING SCALE — 4px base, deliberately non-linear at the top: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 rem (0/4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96/128/192px). Use --s-4 (16px) for paragraph rhythm, --s-6 (32px) between subsections, --s-8 (64px) between major page sections on mobile and --s-9 (96px) on desktop. The jump from 4rem to 6rem to 8rem is what creates the editorial breathing room; a uniform 8px scale produces evenly-grey pages.

TYPE SCALE — progressive ratios, tight at the bottom and expanding at the top, not a single geometric ratio: 0.6875 / 0.75 / 0.8125 / 0.875 / 1.0 / 1.125 / 1.25 / 1.375 / 1.5 / 1.875 / 2.5 / 3.5 / 4.75 rem with line-heights 1.45 / 1.50 / 1.55 / 1.55 / 1.60 / 1.65 / 1.55 / 1.40 / 1.35 / 1.25 / 1.15 / 1.06 / 1.00. The tight bottom end gives four usable metadata sizes (11/12/13/14px) which a publications-and-students site genuinely needs; the expanding top end (ratios 1.25, 1.33, 1.40) gives display type real presence. A uniform 1.25 scale would give you 11px then nothing usable until 21px.

USE SMALL CAPS AND TABULAR FIGURES AS THE SIGNATURE, since self-hosting makes them available: `font-variant-caps: small-caps; letter-spacing: 0.04em` for journal/venue names in the publications list and for section eyebrows ('SELECTED PUBLICATIONS'), and `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the year column, citation counts and any data table. This is the specific detail that will read as 'designed by someone who knows type' and it is invisible-but-felt rather than decorative.

GIVE THE PROFESSOR A CONSTRAINED PALETTE HE CANNOT BREAK. Since content comes from Google Docs/Sheets, strip all inline color, font-family and font-size on import and map only bold/italic/link/heading-level. Expose exactly three authorable flags in the Sheet — a `type` column (journal/conference/preprint/report), a `featured` boolean, and a `tag` free-text — and let the design system decide every visual consequence. If pasted Google Docs styling survives to the page, the site will look templated within a month regardless of how good the type system is.
pitfalls: Linking Google Fonts and then writing `font-variant-caps: small-caps` — it will silently synthesize fake small caps by scaling capitals, which look wrong (too heavy, wrong proportions) and are the classic amateur tell. Google's subset has no smcp table. Same for `font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums`: no onum table, so the declaration does nothing at all and you will think it worked because no error appears.

Using oldstyle figures inside underlined links. The descending 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 collide with the underline and read as subscripts. On a publications page every link contains a year, so this is a site-wide defect. Fix with `font-variant-numeric: lining-nums` scoped to `a`.

Running a subsetter, woff2 converter, or any build-time font pipeline over Fontshare files. ITF FFL v2.0 §02 and §05 explicitly prohibit subsetting and format conversion without prior written consent. Almost every modern web toolchain (next/font, fontaine, glyphhanger, most Astro/Vite font integrations) does exactly this automatically. If you use Fontshare you must ship their shipped .woff2 untouched and disable automatic font optimization.

Pairing a serif and a sans at the same nominal font-size. Public Sans at 18px next to Source Serif 4 at 18px will look noticeably larger because its x-height is 0.517 vs 0.475. Metadata will visually shout over the prose it annotates. Set the sans at 16.5px.

Choosing Fontshare's Erode, Supreme, Bespoke Serif or Synonym for anything containing numbers. They have no tnum feature and non-uniform default digit widths, so a publication-year column will visibly jitter and there is no CSS fix.

Picking a generic tech blue (#0066FF, #2563EB and relatives) as the accent. It is the single most template-coded color on the web, it carries no meaning in this field, and there is a domain-correct alternative sitting in the IPCC's own published colormaps. If a reviewer asks 'why this color', 'it is the IPCC AR6 precipitation ramp' is an answer; 'it looked clean' is not.

Using pure #FFFFFF as the page background and pure #000000 as text. 21:1 contrast produces halation on LCD and is genuinely more tiring for long reading; more practically it is what every unstyled template does. The warm #FBFAF7 / #1B1A17 pair still hits 16.67:1.

Setting the dark-mode background to a pure neutral like #000 or #111 while the light mode is warm. The site will feel like two unrelated designs. Palette A's dark bg #14140F carries the same warm cast as #FBFAF7, which is why the modes read as one identity.

Assuming a hairline at 1.27:1 satisfies WCAG. It does not need to — decorative rules and dividers have no minimum — but the moment that same color is used as a form input border or a toggle edge it falls under SC 1.4.11 and needs 3:1. That is why the spec carries a separate --border-control token at #8F897D (3.33:1 vs bg, 3.08:1 vs surface); using the decorative hairline for inputs is an accessibility failure that automated checkers will catch.

Adding `border-radius: 8px` and a soft drop shadow to publication cards. This combination is the visual fingerprint of Bootstrap/Tailwind-default/AI-generated sites and will undo everything the typography achieves. Hard corners plus a 1px hairline.

Loading the full variable ranges from Google because 'variable fonts are efficient'. Measured, the roman+italic Source Serif 4 pair is 246.2 KB — heavier than most sites' entire JS bundle — and narrowing the requested range does not reduce it by a single byte.

Letting a sticky header cover the focused element. Anchor links from a table of contents will scroll the target under the header and keyboard users will lose focus entirely. This is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (AA) and the fix is one line: `scroll-padding-top`.

Setting prose line-height below about 1.6 at 18px, or letting the measure run past ~75 characters on wide monitors. Both are the standard failure modes of academic sites built from a generic container; 36rem plus 1.65 is the specific combination that works for Source Serif 4.

Choosing Spectral because it looks like a variable font in the specimen. It has zero axes and ships as 14 static files, so every weight you use is another network request and there is no optical-size behavior.

Using EB Garamond from Google Fonts for its small caps and oldstyle figures — the reason most people choose a Garamond. The Google build has neither. It does at least have tnum and tabular defaults, but the Renaissance figure set that justifies the choice is only in the upstream release.

Using two accents where one would do, or letting the secondary accent creep from 'external link marker' into general decoration. The moment #8A5A24 appears as a background tint or an icon color, the palette stops reading as disciplined and starts reading as a theme.

exemplars.name: Gwern Branwen — gwern.net (independent researcher)
exemplars.what_works: The most rigorous type implementation on the public web. Font stacks declared as CSS custom properties with deep, genuinely-considered fallbacks: `--GW-serif-font-stack: "Source Serif 4", "Apple Garamond", "Baskerville", "Libre Baskerville", "Droid Serif", "Times New Roman", "Times", serif`, `--GW-sans-serif-font-stack: "Source Sans 3", ...`, `--GW-monospaced-font-stack: "IBM Plex Mono", ...`. Uses the full OpenType range that only self-hosting allows — font-variant-caps: small-caps and font-variant-numeric switching between oldstyle-nums, lining-nums and tabular-nums by context. Link underlines are not text-decoration at all but a 1px linear-gradient background positioned at `calc(100% - 0.1em)` with `background-size: 1px 1px; background-repeat: repeat-x`, plus a text-shadow halo in the page background color to fake skip-ink with full control.
exemplars.steal_this: The context-switched figure rule. He sets oldstyle figures in running prose for texture, then forces `font-variant-numeric: lining-nums` inside links with the comment '/* Disable oldstyle nums in underlined links because the oldstyle nums are almost subscript-like and overlap */', and tabular-nums in tables. Three different figure styles chosen per context rather than one global setting — that is exactly the discipline a publications-heavy site needs, and it solves a collision bug most designers never notice.

exemplars.name: Kieran Healy — Duke University, Sociology
exemplars.what_works: The reference point for what a serious academic personal site should feel like: single column, austere, content-first, no imagery competing with text, publications as plain linked lists rather than cards. Crucially the typography is commercial and deliberate — the stylesheet resolves to `valkyrie_ot_a` (Matthew Butterick's Valkyrie OT text serif) with `berkeley mono, input-mono-narrow, PragmataPro, Monaco, Menlo, dejavu sans mono, ...` as the monospace stack, and it ships a separate dark.css. A sociologist paying for Butterick and Berkeley Mono is the signal that type choice is doing identity work here.
exemplars.steal_this: The proof that a text-only, image-poor academic site can carry a strong identity purely through one bookish serif plus one engineered monospace, with the mono used for metadata and code rather than as decoration. Source Serif 4 and JetBrains Mono are the zero-cost equivalents of that exact pairing.

exemplars.name: Distill (machine learning research journal)
exemplars.what_works: The most-imitated scientific publishing layout of the last decade. Deliberately conservative type: the stylesheets resolve to `HoeflerText-Regular, Cochin, Georgia, serif` for article body, `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, ...` for UI chrome, and `Consolas, Monaco, 'Andale Mono', 'Ubuntu Mono', monospace` for code. Serif body for the argument, system sans for navigation and figure captions, monospace for data — three faces, three jobs, no overlap.
exemplars.steal_this: The strict role separation: serif owns the argument, sans owns the interface and captions, mono owns data and identifiers. It never lets a face do two jobs. Adopt this allocation directly — serif for bio/blog/abstracts, Public Sans for nav/labels/dates/venue, JetBrains Mono for DOIs, dataset names, code and version numbers.

exemplars.name: IPCC Working Group I — official AR6 colormaps
exemplars.what_works: The authoritative, colorblind-tested color vocabulary for climate and hydrology figures, published as plain RGB text files. Precipitation sequential runs #FFFFE5 to #003C30 through #56A89D / #35978F / #2C877F / #21746B / #166157; precipitation divergent is brown-to-teal #543005 / #F8F8F7 / #003C30; sea level is a separate navy ramp #FEFEFE to #00054A via #2E5995 / #234A8B. The categorical file gree-blue_cat.txt is Paul Tol's colorblind-safe qualitative set verbatim (#332288, #117733, #88CCEE, #999933, #44AA99, #6699CC). The accompanying style guide states the field convention — blue for water, green for biomass, red for temperature — and warns against blue/purple and green/red divergent pairings for colorblind readers.
exemplars.steal_this: The accent color itself, and the argument behind it. Take #166157 (light mode) and #6EB4A7 (dark mode) straight off the AR6 precipitation ramp, and the secondary #8A5A24 from the dry/brown end of the same divergent scale. The site's two accents then literally are the wet and dry poles of his own discipline's visual language — a rationale that survives scrutiny in a way 'we picked a nice teal' does not. Use gree-blue_cat unchanged for any multi-series chart.

exemplars.name: Adobe — Source Serif 4 upstream release

details:
= TYPOGRAPHY & COLOR SPECIFICATION — satishregonda.in

All font facts below were measured from the actual binaries with fontTools 4.64.0, not read off specimen pages. All contrast ratios were computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula; 108 pairs were checked and all pass.

---

## PART 1 — VERIFIED TYPEFACE DATA

### 1.1 The Google Fonts feature-stripping problem (the finding that drives everything)

Diffing Adobe's upstream `SourceSerif4Variable-Roman.otf` against the woff2 Google actually serves:

| | Features present |
|---|---|
| **Upstream (Adobe, OFL)** | aalt **c2sc case** ccmp dnom frac kern liga **lnum** locl mark mkmk numr **onum** ordn pnum sinf **smcp** ss01 ss02 subs sups tnum **zero** |
| **Google-served latin subset** | ccmp dnom frac kern liga locl mark mkmk numr pnum tnum |

13 features removed. Google also strips nameID 13 (the license string) from every family checked — Alegreya, Bitter, Crimson Pro, EB Garamond, Geist, IBM Plex, Inter, Literata, Newsreader, Source Serif 4, Spectral and 24 others all return `NONE-IN-SUBSET`.

**Consequence:** `font-variant-caps: small-caps` and `font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums` are no-ops on Google-hosted fonts. Browsers will *synthesize* small caps by scaling capitals — which is the classic amateur tell.

### 1.2 Figure behaviour, measured from digit advance widths

Tabular by default — all ten digits identical width, publication years align with **no CSS at all**:

| Face | Digit advance | UPM |
|---|---|---|
| Source Serif 4 | 500 | 1000 |
| Spectral | 500 | 1000 |
| Newsreader | 1100 | 2000 |
| EB Garamond | 480 | 1000 |
| Charis SIL | 1153 | 2048 |
| Gentium Book Plus | 986 | 2048 |
| Switzer | 576 | 1000 |
| IBM Plex Serif / Sans / Mono | 600 | 1000 |

Proportional by default **but has `tnum`** (works with one CSS line): Literata (407–578), Lora, Crimson Pro, Petrona, Bitter, Public Sans, Karla, Work Sans, Geist, Inter, Instrument Sans, Space Grotesk, Schibsted Grotesk, Faustina, Vollkorn, Alegreya, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next.

**Neither `tnum` nor tabular defaults — cannot align a year column at all:** Libre Baskerville, Libre Franklin, Fraunces, Instrument Serif, and Fontshare's Erode, Supreme, Bespoke Serif, Synonym, Gambetta.

### 1.3 x-height / cap-height (OS/2 sxHeight, sCapHeight ÷ UPM)

**Serifs:** EB Garamond 0.400 · Crimson Pro 0.420 · Newsreader 0.426 · Petrona 0.443 · Spectral 0.450 · Source Serif 4 0.475 · Fraunces 0.482 · Faustina 0.494 · Lora 0.500 · Sentient 0.504 · Literata 0.507 · Instrument Serif 0.510 · IBM Plex Serif 0.516 · Recia 0.520 · Bitter 0.528 · Libre Baskerville 0.530

**Sans:** Author 0.440 · Karla 0.478 · Space Grotesk 0.486 · Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 0.496 · Satoshi 0.500 · Work Sans 0.500 · Instrument Sans 0.510 · IBM Plex Sans 0.516 · Public Sans 0.517 · Schibsted Grotesk 0.527 · Geist 0.530 · Libre Franklin 0.530 · Switzer 0.531 · General Sans 0.538 · Inter 0.546

**Mono:** IBM Plex Mono 0.516 · Geist Mono 0.530 · JetBrains Mono 0.550

**Size needed to match Source Serif 4 @ 18px (x-height 8.55px):**
Newsreader 20.1px · Spectral 19.0px · Crimson Pro 20.4px · EB Garamond 21.4px · Literata 16.9px · Lora 17.1px · Sentient 17.0px · Recia 16.4px · IBM Plex Serif 16.6px
Public Sans 16.5px · Instrument Sans 16.8px · Schibsted Grotesk 16.2px · Switzer 16.1px · Satoshi 17.1px · JetBrains Mono 15.6px · Geist Mono 16.1px · IBM Plex Mono 16.6px

### 1.4 Measure — average advance per character (em fraction), measured over a real hydrology sentence

Newsreader 0.4097 · Crimson Pro 0.4047 · Spectral 0.4499 · Switzer 0.4517 · **Source Serif 4 0.4562** · Karla 0.4618 · Geist 0.4691 · Public Sans 0.4702 · Lora 0.4714 · Recia 0.4780 · IBM Plex Serif 0.4785 · Literata 0.4881 · Satoshi 0.4903

### 1.5 Variable-font axes and file sizes (Google Fonts metadata endpoint)

| Family | Axes | Italic | Family size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source Serif 4 | opsz 8–60, wght 200–900 | yes | 1008 KB |
| Newsreader | opsz 6–72, wght 200–800 | yes | 463 KB |
| Literata | opsz 7–72, wght 200–900 | yes | 907 KB |
| Fraunces | SOFT 0–100, WONK 0–1, opsz 9–144, wght 100–900 | yes | 379 KB |
| **Spectral** | **none — 14 static styles** | yes | 265 KB |
| Crimson Pro | wght 200–900 | yes | 244 KB |
| EB Garamond | wght 400–800 | yes | 784 KB |
| Public Sans | wght 100–900 | yes | 103 KB |
| Instrument Sans | wdth 75–100, wght 400–700 | yes | 194 KB |
| Geist | wght 100–900 | yes | 168 KB |
| JetBrains Mono | wght 100–800 | yes | 185 KB |
| IBM Plex Sans | wdth 75–100, wght 100–700 | yes | 555 KB |
| Instrument Serif | none — 400/400i only | yes | 69 KB |

### 1.6 Real network payload (measured, latin subset only)

| Request | Files | KB |
|---|---|---|
| Source Serif 4 roman+italic VF, opsz 8–60 wght 200–900 | 2 | **246.2** |
| Public Sans VF wght 100–900, roman | 1 | 26.0 |
| JetBrains Mono VF wght 400–700, roman | 1 | 30.6 |
| **Google-hosted total** | | **302.8** |

Axis-range narrowing does nothing:
- `Source+Serif+4:opsz,wght@8..60,400` → 47.4 KB
- `…@8..60,400..600` → **119.3 KB**
- `…@8..60,200..900` → **119.3 KB** (byte-identical)
- static `wght@400;600` → 99.5 KB (2 files)

Self-hosted, subset to Latin, all features kept:
- opsz variable: 162.2 KB roman / 131.6 KB italic
- **opsz pinned at 20, wght variable: 67.5 KB roman / 53.1 KB italic = 120.6 KB total**

Build command that produced those numbers:
```bash
LAT="U+0020-007E,U+00A0-00FF,U+0131,U+0152-0153,U+2000-200B,U+2010-2027,\
U+2030-205E,U+20AC,U+2122,U+2190-2193,U+2212,U+00B0,U+00D7,U+00B7,U+FEFF,U+FFFD"
FEATS="kern,liga,calt,locl,ccmp,mark,mkmk,tnum,pnum,onum,lnum,smcp,c2sc,\
case,frac,sups,subs,numr,dnom,zero"

python -m fontTools.varLib.instancer \
  SourceSerif4Variable-Roman.otf "opsz=20" -o tmp-roman.otf
python -m fontTools.subset tmp-roman.otf \
  --unicodes="$LAT" --layout-features="$FEATS" \
  --flavor=woff2 --output-file=source-serif-4-roman.woff2
# repeat for SourceSerif4Variable-Italic.otf
```
Verified surviving features: c2sc case ccmp dnom frac kern liga lnum locl mark mkmk numr onum pnum smcp subs sups tnum zero.

### 1.7 Fontshare / Indian Type Foundry — measured

**License: ITF Free Font License (FFL) v2.0, 17 Aug 2026** (read from `Switzer_Complete/License/FFL.txt`).

§01 grants: *"You may self-host the Font Software on your own servers or infrastructure for use on your own websites and applications, including through standard webfont technologies such as CSS @font-face. Self-hosting by end users is permitted and recommended."* Commercial use, unlimited period, no attribution required.

§02 prohibits: *"You may not modify, edit, adapt … This includes modifying or replacing glyphs, **subsetting, format conversion**, or altering font names, copyright information, ownership information or other metadata."*

The Derivative Work definition explicitly names *"subsetting, format conversion"*. §05: no Derivative Work without prior written consent. Governed by Indian law; exclusive jurisdiction Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

**Net effect: ship their .woff2 byte-for-byte, or not at all.** Disable any automatic font optimization in the build (next/font, fontaine, glyphhanger, Vite/Astro font integrations all subset by default).

### 1.8 Google Fonts popularity (the "templated" evidence)

Rank (1 = most used): Roboto 2 · Open Sans 3 · Google Sans 4 · **Inter 5** · Montserrat 7 · Poppins 8 · Lato 9 · Noto Sans JP 10 · Arimo 14 · Roboto Mono 15 · Roboto Condensed 16 · Oswald 19 · Noto Sans 20 · DM Sans 22 · Raleway 23 · Nunito 24 · Nunito Sans 25 · Playfair Display 26 · Roboto Slab 29 · Rubik 30.

Only **two serifs in the top 30**. Leading with a serif is itself a differentiator.

---

## PART 2 — THE THREE PAIRINGS

### PAIRING A — "Gauge" ★ RECOMMENDED

> *A government hydrology report that someone actually designed.*

| Role | Face | Weight | Size / LH |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display | Source Serif 4, `font-variation-settings: 'opsz' 60` | 600 | 3.5rem / 1.06 |
| H1–H3 | Source Serif 4, `'opsz' 36` | 600 | 2.5 / 1.875 / 1.5rem |
| Body | Source Serif 4, `'opsz' 20` | 400 | **1.125rem / 1.65, measure 36rem** |
| Emphasis | Source Serif 4 **true italic** | 400i | — |
| UI / meta | Public Sans | 500 / 600 | **1.03125rem (16.5px)** — x-height matched |
| Mono | JetBrains Mono | 400 | 0.9688rem (15.5px) — x-height matched |

Licences: Source Serif 4 — SIL OFL 1.1, © Adobe, RFN "Source", github.com/adobe-fonts/source-serif. Public Sans — OFL, USWDS. JetBrains Mono — OFL.
Payload self-hosted: 120.6 KB serif + ~26 KB Public Sans + ~31 KB JetBrains Mono ≈ **178 KB**.

Why it wins: one superfamily means hierarchy comes from **optical size**, not from a zoo of faces — exactly the move a foundry makes and a template cannot. Tabular by default. Self-hosting restores small caps + oldstyle figures. It is the stack gwern.net uses.

### PAIRING B — "Estuary"

> *Broadsheet science journalism — literary, high-contrast, confident.*

| Role | Face | Weight | Size / LH |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display | Newsreader, `'opsz' 72` | 500 | 3.5rem / 1.06 |
| Standfirst | Newsreader **Italic**, `'opsz' 36` | 400i | 1.5rem / 1.4 |
| Body | Newsreader, `'opsz' 16` | 400 | **1.25rem (20px) / 1.6, measure 34rem** |
| UI / meta | Schibsted Grotesk | 500 | 1.0139rem (16.2px) |
| Mono | Geist Mono | 400 | 1.0081rem (16.1px) |

Newsreader: Production Type, OFL, opsz **6–72** (the widest optical range of any free text serif), true italics, **tabular by default** (1100/2000), 463 KB family. Its 0.426 x-height is small — it *must* run at 20px. The wide opsz range gives genuinely different display and text designs.
Risk: 20px body plus a 34rem measure is a committed, literary look. Less institutionally neutral than A.

### PAIRING C — "Deccan" (Indian foundry route)

> *Contemporary Indian editorial — warm, sharp, unmistakably not a template.*

| Role | Face | Weight | Size / LH |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display | Boska (has real `smcp`) | 700 | 3.5rem / 1.06 |
| H1–H3 | Recia | 600 | 2.5 / 1.875 / 1.5rem |
| Body | Recia | 400 | **1.0625rem (17px) / 1.65, measure 35.5rem** |
| UI / meta | Switzer (tabular by default) | 500 | 1.0063rem (16.1px) |
| Mono | JetBrains Mono (OFL — Fontshare has no true mono) | 400 | 0.9688rem |

Recia is the only Fontshare serif with a complete figure set (tnum, pnum, onum, lnum, zero, case). Switzer's uniform 576/1000 digits align publication years for free. Boska is the only Fontshare face with real small caps.
**Hard constraint:** FFL v2.0 forbids subsetting/conversion — ship ITF's woff2 untouched (~34.7 + 42 + 42.2 + 33 + 46.2 KB ≈ 198 KB, no build-time optimization possible). Genuine, non-decorative Indian design provenance.

### Type scale (shared by all three)

| Token | rem | px | LH | Line box | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--fs-3xs` | 0.6875 | 11 | 1.45 | 15.9px | micro label, figure credit |
| `--fs-2xs` | 0.75 | 12 | 1.50 | 18.0px | dates, venue, DOI, counts |
| `--fs-xs` | 0.8125 | 13 | 1.55 | 20.2px | captions, footnotes, table cells |
| `--fs-sm` | 0.875 | 14 | 1.55 | 21.7px | UI labels, nav, buttons |
| `--fs-base` | 1.0 | 16 | 1.60 | 25.6px | dense lists, publication entries |
| `--fs-body` | 1.125 | 18 | 1.65 | 29.7px | **prose body** |
| `--fs-lead` | 1.25 | 20 | 1.55 | 31.0px | lead paragraph |
| `--fs-h4` | 1.375 | 22 | 1.40 | 30.8px | h4 / card title |
| `--fs-h3` | 1.5 | 24 | 1.35 | 32.4px | section subhead |
| `--fs-h2` | 1.875 | 30 | 1.25 | 37.5px | section head |
| `--fs-h1` | 2.5 | 40 | 1.15 | 46.0px | page title |
| `--fs-display` | 3.5 | 56 | 1.06 | 59.4px | hero |
| `--fs-mega` | 4.75 | 76 | 1.00 | 76.0px | desktop hero only |

Ratios are **progressive**, not uniform: 1.091 → 1.083 → 1.077 → 1.143 → 1.125 → 1.111 → 1.100 → 1.091 → **1.250 → 1.333 → 1.400 → 1.357**. Tight at the bottom gives four usable metadata sizes (11/12/13/14px) that a publications-and-students site genuinely needs; expanding at the top gives display type presence. A uniform 1.25 scale would give 11px then nothing usable until 21px.

## PART 3 — COLOR

### PALETTE A — "Gauge" ★ RECOMMENDED (warm paper + IPCC precipitation teal)

The two accents are literally the **wet and dry poles of his own field's visual language**. The warm paper #FBFAF7 echoes the ramp's #FFFFE5 dry end.

Laterite red is the soil colour of the Deccan; the teal secondary keeps the IPCC water link. Warmest and most distinctive — but red reads as *alert* in a flood-forecasting context, which is a real semantic risk.

### Accent usage rules (all palettes)

**`--accent` may be used ONLY for:**
1. Inline text links in prose
2. The active nav item's underline
3. The focus ring
4. One thin rule or marker on the current section heading
5. Small-caps status tags (NEW / PREPRINT / IN REVIEW)

**Never:** large filled areas, hero backgrounds, card backgrounds, non-link icons, decorative dividers, section backgrounds. Those use `--hairline` and `--text-2`.

**`--accent-2`** has exactly one job: marking outbound links (raftwaters.in, DOIs, journal pages). More than one accent-2 mark per screen is a bug.

**Budget:** accent should occupy roughly ≤2% of painted pixels on any page.

### Charts

Use IPCC `gree-blue_cat` (Paul Tol colorblind-safe) unchanged: `#332288 #117733 #88CCEE #999933 #44AA99 #6699CC`. Sequential hydrology data: the AR6 prec ramp `#FFFFE5 #C6E2CD #8EC5B5 #56A89D #2C877F #166157 #003C30`. Divergent (anomaly): `#543005 #BF812C #E5D1B4 #F8F8F7 #B7D8D5 #35978F #003C30`.

```css
--s-9:6rem; --s-10:8rem; --s-11:12rem;
```
0/4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96/128/192px. `--s-4` paragraph rhythm · `--s-6` between subsections · `--s-8` major sections (mobile) · `--s-9` major sections (desktop). The 4→6→8rem jumps create the editorial breathing room; a uniform 8px scale yields evenly-grey pages.

### Grid & widths
```css
--w-prose:36rem;    /* 576px — ~70ch in Source Serif 4 @18px */
--w-content:48rem;  /* 768px — publication lists, student tables */
--w-wide:76rem;     /* 1216px — hero, RAFT image grid */
```
- ≥1024px: 12 columns, 24px gutters, inside `--w-wide`
- 768–1023px: 6 columns, 20px gutters
- <768px: 1 column, 20px page margins

**Prose runs *outside* the grid** — `max-width: var(--w-prose); margin-inline: auto`. Only figures/tables/image strips opt into full width via a `.bleed` utility. Academic pages are ~90% single-column text; imposing a grid on paragraphs fights the measure.

### Radii
```css
--r-0:0;      /* cards, sections, images, prose container — DEFAULT */
--r-1:2px;    /* tags, chips, code spans */
--r-2:4px;    /* form inputs and buttons only */
--r-full:999px; /* avatar only */
```
Rounded cards are the loudest "template" signal on the web. Hard corners + 1px `--hairline` is what a printed journal does.

### Shadows
**None on static content.** Structure = hairlines + surface/bg split. Two exceptions, transient overlays only:
```css
--shadow-pop: 0 1px 2px rgb(27 26 23 / .06), 0 4px 12px rgb(27 26 23 / .08);
--shadow-modal: 0 8px 40px rgb(27 26 23 / .16);
```
In **dark mode replace both with a 1px `--hairline` top border** — shadows are invisible on #14140F and the border is what actually reads as elevation.

### Focus
```css
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--focus);
  outline-offset: 2px;
  border-radius: 2px;
}
:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none; }
html { scroll-padding-top: 5rem; }   /* WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 */
```
Verified 6.98:1 vs bg, 6.45:1 vs surface (light); 7.70:1 / 7.05:1 (dark) — well past the 3:1 that **SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA)** requires. Outline is **outset**, so 2px satisfies **SC 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA)** area rule; an *inset* indicator would need 3px. `scroll-padding-top` prevents the sticky header obscuring anchor targets (**SC 2.4.11, AA**).

### Links — the highest-leverage decision on a link-dense academic site
```css
a {
  color: var(--accent);
  text-decoration: underline;
  text-decoration-thickness: 0.06em;
  text-underline-offset: 0.16em;
  text-decoration-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 40%, transparent);
  text-decoration-skip-ink: auto;
  font-variant-numeric: lining-nums;  /* CRITICAL — see below */
  transition: text-decoration-color .12s ease, color .12s ease;
}
a:hover {
  text-decoration-color: var(--accent);
  text-decoration-thickness: 0.09em;
  color: var(--accent-hover);
}
a:visited { color: var(--visited); }
a[href^="http"]:not([href*="satishregonda.in"])::after {
  content: "↗"; color: var(--accent-2);
  font-size: .75em; margin-inline-start: .15em;
  vertical-align: .15em; text-decoration: none;
}
```
- **em units** so the underline scales with type size.
- **`font-variant-numeric: lining-nums` on `a` is mandatory.** Oldstyle figures descend below the baseline and collide with the underline. gwern's source comment: *"Disable oldstyle nums in underlined links because the oldstyle nums are almost subscript-like and overlap."* On a publications page every link contains a year.
- If finer control is needed, use gwern's technique: a 1px `linear-gradient` background at `background-position: 0% calc(100% - 0.1em); background-size: 1px 1px; background-repeat: repeat-x`, plus a `text-shadow` halo in `--bg` to fake skip-ink.

**Underlines removed in exactly three places**, each with a replacement affordance:
1. **Nav** — active state = 2px accent underline at 0.4em offset
2. **Publication list** — hover-only underline on titles (60 underlined lines in a row is unreadable)
3. **Cards** — whole-card hover moves surface `#FBFAF7` → `#F3F1EB`

Everywhere else in prose: **always underline.**

### Signature OpenType details (only available self-hosted)
```css
.venue, .eyebrow {            /* journal names, "SELECTED PUBLICATIONS" */
  font-variant-caps: small-caps;
  letter-spacing: .04em;
}
.pub-year, .metrics, table td { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
p { font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums; }   /* texture in running prose */
a { font-variant-numeric: lining-nums; }      /* override — collision fix */
```

### CMS guardrail
Content arrives from Google Docs/Sheets. **Strip all inline color, font-family and font-size on import**; map only bold, italic, link and heading level. Expose exactly three authorable fields in the Sheet — `type` (journal/conference/preprint/report), `featured` (boolean), `tag` (free text) — and let the design system decide every visual consequence. If pasted Google Docs styling survives to the page, the site will look templated within a month regardless of how good the type system is.
